title: ADPKD: bilateral renal cysts + hepatic cysts
vignette: A 54-year-old man comes to the physician due to blood in his urine and abdominal discomfort that occurred 2 days ago. He was moving potted plants around his porch when he started having pain in his abdomen. Afterward, he noticed blood in his urine but says it resolved the following day. He has a history of hypertension. The patient does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. CT scan of the abdomen with contrast shows multiple bilateral renal cysts with thin, nonenhancing walls, along with several hepatic cysts. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

clues.text: abdominal discomfort that occurred 2 days ago
clues.note: Flank/abdominal pain (often after exertion) results from stretching of the renal capsule or cyst rupture in polycystic kidneys.

clues.text: noticed blood in his urine but says it resolved
clues.note: Transient gross hematuria in ADPKD occurs when a cyst ruptures into the collecting system.
Hypertension is often the EARLIEST clinical sign of ADPKD (from cyst-related renin activation).

clues.text: multiple bilateral renal cysts with thin, nonenhancing walls, along with several hepatic cysts
clues.note: Multiple BILATERAL thin-walled nonenhancing renal cysts PLUS hepatic cysts are diagnostic of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.

whatMatters: Flank pain + transient hematuria + hypertension + multiple BILATERAL renal cysts and HEPATIC cysts on CT = autosomal dominant POLYCYSTIC KIDNEY DISEASE (ADPKD). Answer D. ADPKD (PKD1/PKD2 mutations) causes progressive cystic enlargement, hypertension, hematuria, liver cysts, and berry (intracranial) aneurysms.
strategy: Recognize the ADPKD triad: bilateral renal cysts + extrarenal cysts (liver) + hypertension/hematuria in an adult. Reject glomerulonephritis (RBC casts, no cysts), hydronephrosis (dilated collecting system from obstruction), nephroblastoma/Wilms (pediatric solid mass), and renal cell carcinoma (solitary ENHANCING solid mass with necrosis, not bilateral thin-walled cysts).

eliminations.label: Glomerulonephritis - no cysts; casts
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: glomerular inflammation causing hematuria, hypertension, and renal failure. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it shows RBC casts/proteinuria on urinalysis, not multiple bilateral cysts with hepatic cysts. ✅ Correct if: hematuria with dysmorphic RBCs/casts and no cysts.

eliminations.label: Hydronephrosis - dilated collecting system (obstruction)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: dilation of the renal pelvis/calyces from obstruction (e.g., a stone). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: imaging would show dilated ureters/calyces, not multiple discrete cysts plus liver cysts. ✅ Correct if: obstructive uropathy with hydronephrosis.

eliminations.label: Nephroblastoma - Wilms tumor (pediatric)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the most common pediatric renal malignancy, presenting as a solid painful abdominal mass. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is rare in adults and appears as a solid heterogeneous mass, not bilateral cysts. ✅ Correct if: a young child with a palpable abdominal mass + hematuria.

eliminations.label: Renal cell carcinoma - solitary enhancing solid mass (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the most common adult renal malignancy (hematuria, flank pain, hypertension). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: RCC typically shows a SOLITARY solid, contrast-ENHANCING mass with necrosis - not multiple bilateral thin-walled cysts and liver cysts. ✅ Correct if: a solitary enhancing renal mass (RCC).

reasoning: Adult with flank pain + transient hematuria + hypertension
CT shows multiple BILATERAL thin-walled renal cysts plus hepatic cysts
This constellation is diagnostic of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
mechanism: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is the most common HEREDITARY cause of renal failure in adults, due to mutations in the POLYCYSTIN genes (PKD1 on chromosome 16, or PKD2). Countless fluid-filled cysts progressively enlarge and replace both kidneys. Patients are often asymptomatic until the 4th-5th decade, when cyst growth impairs renal function; HYPERTENSION is frequently the earliest sign (activation of the renin-angiotensin system). Stretching of the renal capsule and cyst rupture cause abdominal/FLANK PAIN and gross HEMATURIA (as here, often after exertion). Extrarenal manifestations include HEPATIC cysts (and pancreatic/splenic cysts), berry (intracranial) ANEURYSMS that can rupture -> subarachnoid hemorrhage, and mitral valve prolapse; roughly half progress to end-stage renal disease by ~age 60-70. CT shows multiple bilateral thin-walled, nonenhancing cysts - contrasting with the solitary ENHANCING solid mass of renal cell carcinoma, the casts of glomerulonephritis, the dilated system of hydronephrosis, and the solid pediatric mass of Wilms tumor.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Renal > ADPKD: PKD1/PKD2 mutations; bilateral renal cysts, hypertension, hematuria, flank pain; hepatic cysts, berry aneurysms, mitral valve prolapse; progressive renal failure.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Bilateral thin-walled renal cysts + hepatic cysts + hypertension/hematuria = ADPKD (not a solid tumor).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on ADPKD, polycystin/PKD1-2, berry aneurysm, or cyst vs solid mass on imaging? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: RCC = solitary enhancing solid mass; glomerulonephritis = casts; hydronephrosis = dilated system; Wilms = pediatric solid mass.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the contrast CT: both kidneys are enlarged and studded with numerous thin-walled, nonenhancing (fluid) cysts, with cysts also in the liver. Anchor: 'bilateral renal cysts + liver cysts = ADPKD.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: ADPKD = bilateral renal cysts + hepatic cysts + hypertension + hematuria; berry aneurysms; PKD1/PKD2.

keywords.front: Bilateral renal cysts + hepatic cysts + hypertension/hematuria

keywords.back: Solitary enhancing solid mass with necrosis
Hepatic/pancreatic cysts, mitral valve prolapse, colonic diverticula

firstAid.detail: Renal: PKD1/PKD2; bilateral renal + hepatic cysts; hypertension, hematuria, berry aneurysms.
Renal > RCC (solid enhancing), glomerulonephritis (casts), hydronephrosis, Wilms (peds).
Renal > progressive ESRD; screen for intracranial aneurysm if indicated.

memoryHook: Two kidneys full of bubbles plus a bubbly liver in a hypertensive adult with bloody urine = ADPKD (and beware the berry aneurysm in the brain).
